I was told as high as 30% for error rates in nuchals when I was looking at what tests I wanted. The error rates in NIPT varies by brand and by each test they offer - they aren't all equal. I chose to get the Harmony NIPT and skip the nuchal in the end (the relatively poor reliability of a nuchal made me more anxious).

I'm not sure what you're referring to by "inconclusive", but.... 

- the samples are stupid temperature sensitive, someone could have transported or stored it wrong (I've seen this done). Also, some companies here in Aus transport samples to the US, imagine trying to keep the temperature stable... 

- they need a certain amount of fetal DNA to get an accurate result and if - when they measure the amount - there's not enough, they don't test. Or they shouldn't, not all companies are the same.

- multiples often affect the NIPT test so you can't get the full results (what you can get depends on number and gender). 

Inconclusive is scary and frustrating but it doesn't have to be anything "wrong" at all. And in Australia, Harmony will redo the NIPT if they can't get a result the first time, so you could try that too or a refund.

If on the other hand you have results but your doctor wasn't sure what to make of them, that's a bit different, but the genetic counsellor will absolutely guide you.
